episode.title: Broaden approved-command writes without weakening explicit filesystem denials
episode.before: At parent de9e78e3e7caed0fdd75d20ae617faa646dfef3c, the policy layer had no operation for deriving an approved-command policy that granted filesystem-root writes while retaining only explicit denial restrictions. Linux sandbox translation used ordinary writable and unreadable root resolution, rebound every resolved writable root or root alias, and did not recreate the minimal device tree after binding `/`; consequently a broad root bind could shadow standard devices, while extra metadata or alias binds could undo masks or reopen denied symlink targets. Executor capabilities did not describe support for preserving devices or restrictions during Linux root writes.
episode.after: At 645b683a9e712ae6d90a364e3cf597466e4146d0, approved commands can derive a restricted policy that writes the filesystem root and non-denied root metadata while preserving explicit path and glob read denials. Unsafe or unresolvable denials cause conservative fallback to the original policy. Linux mount planning inherits metadata writes from a writable root, retains literal denial paths alongside resolved targets, avoids redundant root-alias binds, recreates standard devices after binding `/`, and applies explicit deny masks afterward. Two opt-in capability fields advertise the Linux guarantees without changing legacy false-valued serialization.
episode.diff: The commit changes nine Rust files with 780 insertions and 12 deletions. It adds approved-policy derivation and cross-platform materialization tests; adds Linux-specific writable-root and unreadable-root resolution modes; changes bubblewrap mount ordering and root-alias behavior; adds end-to-end tests for standard devices, denied metadata symlink targets, and Windows volume expansion; and adds backward-compatible executor capability fields and serialization tests.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned commit has parent de9e78e3e7caed0fdd75d20ae617faa646dfef3c and states that approved commands require broader write access while retaining explicit read denials; it reports 780 insertions and 12 deletions across nine files.

The new approved-command transformation starts from a restricted root-write policy, copies deny-read restrictions, materializes project-root references, and adds writes for non-denied protected root metadata.

The transformation returns the original policy for non-restricted policies and conservatively falls back when workspace-dependent denials lack roots, materialization or matcher construction fails, the filesystem root cannot be determined, or the root itself is denied or not writable.
The parent Linux translator used get_writable_roots_with_cwd and get_unreadable_roots_with_cwd, then unconditionally emitted a bind for every resolved writable mount root.
evidence_units.source: git show de9e78e3e7caed0fdd75d20ae617faa646dfef3c:codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs; create_filesystem_args around writable/unreadable root collection and writable bind emission

evidence_units.claim: Linux writable-root resolution can now omit separate protected-metadata mounts when the filesystem root is writable, preventing a metadata symlink mount from reopening a target beneath an explicit denial.
Linux unreadable-root resolution now includes qualifying literal deny paths as well as resolved targets, allowing enforcement to reject traversal through a writable symlink.

The bubblewrap argument builder consumes the new Linux-specific writable and unreadable root projections, suppresses redundant aliases resolving to `/`, recreates `/dev` and `/dev/shm` after a root bind, and then applies explicit masks.

Policy tests cover Unix, Windows-drive, and UNC contexts; verify root and allowed metadata writes; verify retained path and glob denials; discard unrelated prior grants; and require unchanged-policy fallback for root or unresolvable denials.
A Linux integration test derives an approved policy, verifies standard device reads and ordinary output writes still work, and verifies reading an explicitly denied file fails with permission denied.

A Linux integration test verifies root-metadata symlinks cannot reopen denied targets, allowed metadata writes still work, writable-symlink crossings are rejected, and an explicit nested writable carveout does not expose denied siblings.

A Windows-oriented policy test verifies approved-command volume-root expansion removes former grants, preserves denials, permits volume roots, and retains the intended distinction between denied root metadata and workspace metadata.
The executor protocol adds two default-false, false-omitting capability flags and reports both as supported only on Linux.

Capability tests verify false fields are absent from legacy serialization, partial support defaults the other field to false, true-valued fields round-trip, and local values match the target operating system.
The commit supplies unit and integration regression oracles, but the available evidence bundle contains no CI status or recorded test execution result.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json limitations and pull_request.metadata_unavailable; pinned commit test changes

candidate_atomics.name: derive-broadened-policy-with-denial-retention
candidate_atomics.title: Derive a broader approved policy while retaining explicit denials
candidate_atomics.description: Construct the least restrictive approved-command policy needed for broad writes, retain explicit read-denial invariants, discard unrelated old grants, and fail closed to the original policy when denials cannot be safely resolved.

semantic_action.intent: Permit an explicitly approved command to write broadly without allowing it to read paths or globs that the original policy explicitly denied.
semantic_action.pre_state: A command has a filesystem policy and execution context; approval requires broader writes, while explicit denial entries may contain concrete, workspace-relative, or glob paths.
semantic_action.post_state: A restricted root-write policy retains materializable explicit read denials and grants only non-denied protected metadata writes; unsafe or unresolved cases retain the original policy unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Compare resolved access and deny matching across Unix, drive-letter, UNC, project-root, glob, metadata, and multi-volume cases; assert conservative identity fallback for root-level or unresolved denials.

candidate_atomics.name: compile-root-write-policy-with-isolated-denials
candidate_atomics.title: Compile broad root writes without reopening denied effects
candidate_atomics.description: Translate the broadened policy into mount operations whose ordering preserves standard devices and prevents aliases, metadata symlinks, or resolved-path handling from bypassing explicit denial masks.

semantic_action.intent: Execute a broad-write policy while keeping standard operating-system devices usable and explicit denial boundaries effective through symlinks and mount aliases.
semantic_action.pre_state: The sandbox receives a policy containing a writable filesystem root plus explicit denied carveouts; aliases or protected metadata entries may resolve into the root or denied subtrees.
semantic_action.post_state: The root is writable, the minimal device tree is restored, redundant root aliases and metadata remounts do not undo masks, literal and resolved denial paths are enforced, and only explicit nested writable carveouts reopen access.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect mount-plan ordering and run sandboxed commands that access standard devices, write allowed outputs and metadata, fail on denied reads, reject writable-symlink crossings, and keep denied sibling paths inaccessible.

candidate_atomics.name: advertise-opt-in-isolation-guarantees
candidate_atomics.title: Advertise isolation guarantees without breaking legacy peers
candidate_atomics.description: Expose independently detectable support for root-write device preservation and approved-root restriction preservation, with false values omitted for wire compatibility.

semantic_action.intent: Let clients select broad-root behavior only when the executor declares the required safety guarantees.
semantic_action.pre_state: Clients cannot distinguish executors that safely preserve devices and denial restrictions during Linux root writes from executors lacking those guarantees.
semantic_action.post_state: Executors expose two independent opt-in guarantees; absent fields deserialize as false and false values remain absent from legacy-compatible serialization.
semantic_action.validation: Serialize default, partial, and full capability values; deserialize each supported form; and compare locally advertised values with the target platform.

candidate_workflows.name: broaden-approved-effects-with-explicit-denial-isolation
candidate_workflows.title: Broaden approved filesystem effects while preserving denial boundaries
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for granting broad write effects to an approved command without inheriting unrelated grants or allowing mount translation, devices, aliases, or metadata symlinks to weaken explicit read denials.

workflow_graph.goal: Run an approved command with broad filesystem write authority while preserving every enforceable explicit read denial and making the platform guarantee discoverable to clients.
when_to_use: An approval transition must broaden a restricted command from scoped writes to filesystem-root or volume-root writes.
The sandbox represents explicit denied paths or globs that must survive the approval transition.
The platform implements broad access through bind mounts, volume expansion, or comparable remapping that can shadow devices or reopen aliased targets.
anti_goals: Do not retain unrelated read or write grants from the pre-approval policy.
Do not silently drop, weaken, or reinterpret an explicit denial to make broad approval succeed.
Do not bind aliases or protected metadata paths redundantly when doing so can undo an already-applied denial mask.
Do not advertise a safety guarantee on platforms or executors that do not implement it.
not_applicable_when: Approval does not broaden filesystem effects.
The policy has no restricted-mode transformation or no explicit denial semantics to preserve.
The execution backend does not remap roots, volumes, aliases, or device trees and cannot exhibit the documented reopening or shadowing failure modes.
Required denials are intentionally revoked by a separately authorized policy decision rather than preserved through approval.
workflow_graph.entry_state: The command's current policy limits writes and may explicitly deny reads; approval requires broader writes, but no safe broadened policy or advertised execution guarantee has yet been established.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The approved command can perform intended broad writes and use required standard devices, explicit denials remain effective through aliases and metadata symlinks, unsafe transformations fall back instead of widening access, and compatible clients can detect the implemented guarantee.

steps.condition: Run when approval requires broader filesystem writes under a restricted policy.
steps.validation: Policy-level tests prove retained path and glob denials, removed unrelated grants, allowed root and metadata writes, cross-platform root materialization, and unchanged-policy fallback for unsafe inputs.

steps.condition: Run for a backend whose root, volume, alias, metadata, or device remapping can change the effective policy.
steps.validation: Mount-plan and integration tests prove device restoration occurs after the root bind and before explicit masks, aliases do not rebind the root, metadata symlinks cannot reopen denied targets, and explicit carveouts behave narrowly.

steps.condition: Run when clients or remote peers choose behavior based on executor support.
steps.validation: Wire tests prove default omission, false-on-absence compatibility, independent partial support, full round-trip behavior, and platform-correct local advertisement.

validation_ladder: Policy transformation: assert exact approved entries, resolved access, deny matching, removal of prior grants, and fail-closed fallback.
Platform projection: assert writable roots, protected-metadata handling, literal denial retention, volume expansion, alias suppression, and mount ordering.
Sandbox integration: execute device reads, allowed writes, denied reads, metadata-symlink attempts, writable-symlink crossings, and narrow nested carveouts.
Protocol compatibility: verify absent, partial, and full capability serialization and platform-specific advertisement.
Run the relevant Rust unit and Linux integration test targets in an environment with bubblewrap/user-namespace support; the bundle does not provide an execution result.
stop_conditions: Stop and keep the original policy if a workspace-relative denial lacks workspace roots, denial materialization or matching fails, the filesystem root cannot be identified, or the root is explicitly denied.
Stop promotion if broad root writes can shadow required devices or any alias or metadata mount can reopen a denied target.
Stop capability advertisement unless the corresponding device and denial-preservation behaviors are implemented and validated.
Defer execution-level confirmation when the host cannot run bubblewrap or create the required user namespace.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle has no CI status, review record, or recorded test-run result; validation is grounded in added test oracles rather than observed execution.
The pinned change introduces and directly tests approved-policy derivation, but the inspected evidence does not establish a non-test production caller that invokes the new transformation.
Client-side consumption of the two new capability fields is outside this commit and remains deferred.

unresolved_questions: Were the added Rust unit and Linux bubblewrap integration tests executed successfully for the pinned commit? The supplied GitHub bundle omits status checks.
Which production approval path is intended to invoke the new approved-command policy transformation? The pinned change demonstrates direct test call sites but does not establish that integration.
Which clients consume the new executor capability flags, and what fallback behavior do they use when the fields are absent?
